entries.name: Cook's Assistant
entries.summary: The head cook of Lumbridge Castle forgot to buy the ingredients for Duke Horacio's birthday cake and roped in the first adventurer through the kitchen door. That was you. He kept his job, and you got the use of his range.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.body:
You walked into the castle kitchen and found the head cook in a panic. It was the Duke's birthday, the cook was meant to be baking the cake, and he had forgotten to buy the ingredients. He was certain the Duke would sack him, and he had four children and a goat to feed. His words; I have a note on the goat further down.

The list was a bucket of milk, an egg and a pot of flour. He sent you to Millie Miller for the flour, Gillie Groats for the milk, and the Groats' farm or any chicken for the egg. Any chicken. He was past being particular.

The egg first, from the chicken coop. Nothing to it. Then the milk: you took an empty bucket into the cow field and used it on the dairy cow. Gillie Groats will explain milking if asked; it is a cow and a bucket, but the offer stands.

Then the flour, which took the most steps. You picked grain in the wheat field, tipped it into the hopper at Mill Lane Mill, pulled the lever, and filled an empty pot from the flour bin. Millie Miller explains how it works, should the lever not explain itself.

You brought all three back and the cook declared himself saved. You asked whether you could come to the Duke's party. He said only important people dine with nobility, and that perhaps one day you would be one of them, though he doubted it. I have underlined 'doubted'.

Then he let you use his range. He calls it the Cook-o-matic 100, and it burns fewer foods than an ordinary range. Somebody in that kitchen needed to.

sections.heading: Who was there
sections.body:
The cook, described, with no great effort, as "The head cook of Lumbridge castle." As for the goat: he claims one, along with a wife and four children, and Bob the cat contradicts him.

Duke Horacio, the Duke of Lumbridge, whose birthday it was. Never seen during the quest; he lives on the first floor of the castle, one floor up from the trouble.

sections.heading: Where it took us
sections.body:
Lumbridge Castle kitchen, ground floor. The cook, his range, and a pot that is always on the centre table.

Lumbridge Castle cellar, down the kitchen trapdoor. There is always a bucket.

The chicken coop: east out of the castle, north up the path, north-west of Farmer Fred's house. That house was the whole of Fred's part. The egg.

The Lumbridge cow field, across the River Lum. The dairy cow with the cowbell, and Gillie Groats beside it.

The wheat field south-west of the cow field. The grain.

Mill Lane Mill. Hopper and lever on the top floor, flour bin on the ground floor, Millie Miller inside.

Lumbridge General Store. Buckets and pots, if you arrive with neither.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
The errand sends you all round Lumbridge. A shopping list doing the work of a map. It works.

The cook has form. It came out later that he has tried and failed to bake a cake countless times.

{done:DEATH_TO_THE_DORGESHUUN} In Death to the Dorgeshuun, when you introduce Zanik to him, he tries to offer her the very same errand. You tell him she has no time and he says it was worth a try.

The histories take this to mean he asks every newcomer. I take it the same way. The cook at the Servants' Guild in Ardougne complains that she was fired overnight and replaced by a fool who cannot bake a cake without help. The description fits.

{done:RECIPE_FOR_DISASTER__ANOTHER_COOKS_QUEST} The kitchen has history. The cook's ancestor Franizzard Van Lumbcook won the post of head cook for life a century ago by impressing the Lumbridge council with a banquet.

{done:RECIPE_FOR_DISASTER} Recipe for Disaster follows on from this one. The cook tries to recreate that banquet for the council's ten-yearly meeting, and the Culinaromancer, a hostile cook trapped in another dimension a hundred years earlier, crashes the feast.

Lumbridge itself was settled by human nomads who bridged the River Lum, which is where the name comes from. The rest, from the first Duke onward, is on the Lumbridge page. Nobody in the kitchen brought it up.

On the range. Adventurers call it the Lumbridge Castle range. The foods it burns less often run from bread and shrimps up to salmon, and it is especially good for mushroom and botanical pies.

Bob the cat praises the cook's old fashioned seafood gumbo, an old family recipe. So the man can cook. He cannot bake, which is a different complaint.

One last note. You can buy all three ingredients on the Grand Exchange before talking to the cook and finish the quest in seconds. Which rather defeats the map.

people: Gillie Groats - the milkmaid, optional
Millie Miller - the miller, optional; of the two explanations, hers is worth hearing
details: Reward - 1 quest point
Reward - 300 Cooking experience
Reward - the use of the Cook-o-matic 100

plates.caption: Lumbridge, where it began.
plates.hint: Stop in Lumbridge and I'll draw it.

entries.name: Priest in Peril
entries.summary: King Roald sent you to check on Drezel, the priest at Paterdomus, because the temple had gone quiet. Monks of Zamorak had taken it, and they talked you into killing the Temple Guardian so they could poison the Salve.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.body:
Paterdomus is the temple to Saradomin on Misthalin's eastern border. King Roald told you the blessed waters of the River Salve beneath it are what keep the vampyres of Morytania out.

Nobody had heard from Drezel, and Roald asked you to go and check on him. I wrote down 'check'. It turned out to be a small word for the job.

At the temple door a voice asked who you were and what you wanted. When you said the King had sent you, a second voice introduced itself as Drevil, then hurriedly corrected that to Drezel. I wrote 'Drevil' down with a question mark, and nobody consulted the notes.

This so-called Drezel said a horrible big dog-like thing had moved into the mausoleum outside and asked you to get rid of it. You killed the Temple Guardian down there, "a big ugly dog" by common account. The description was unkind; so, in the end, were we. The dog has its own page.

Back at the palace, King Roald was furious. The dog was no pest: it guarded the mausoleum entrance and the source of the Salve, and with it dead anyone could sabotage the river's blessing.

He called it treason and threatened to have you beheaded, then relented and ordered you to put it right. I took those minutes very quietly.

Back inside the temple you fought the hooded monk, who casts spells, though there is a spot between the pews he cannot reach you in, and took the golden key he dropped. The monks have their own page.

Upstairs was the real Drezel, locked in a cell. Through the bars he told you Zamorakians had attacked the temple to desecrate the blessing the Seven Priestly Warriors had placed on the Salve, and had brought a trapped vampyre up into a coffin near his cell. The golden key did not fit his door; the real one was hidden somewhere.

In the mausoleum again, the golden key opened the room of seven monuments round the well. Searching them turned up the iron key, which you swapped for the golden one. You filled a bucket with murky water from the well, and murky was the polite word.

The iron key opened Drezel's cell. He blessed the water and you poured it over the coffin outside his cell, sealing the vampyre inside. It did not thank you.

Below, Drezel explained that the Zamorakians had used a potion to pollute the Salve. While he reinforced the barrier, you were to soak up the evil magic it had released, with essence. Hand him the essence outright and he skips the speech; what gets written is that you gave the priest your blank runes, which I have not corrected.

When it was done he gave you Wolfbane, a silver dagger passed down through his family for generations and imbued with the power of Saradomin. The dagger gets its own paragraph further down. It earned it.

He warned of the vampyres and werewolves beyond and mentioned the Myreque resistance. To cross, you ask him for permission to pass and wait for his blessing; he is a priest, and there is a form.

sections.heading: Who was there
sections.body:
King Roald: King Roald Remanis III, ruler of Misthalin, in Varrock Palace, married to Queen Ellamaria, who calls the dog Spots. The histories call him a straightforward, stable ruler under whom Varrock has prospered.

Drezel: described, and briefly, as "A holy man." A priest of Saradomin, descended from one of the Seven Priestly Warriors. Use a spare iron key on his old cell door and he asks what you are trying to lock him back in for, which is a fair question.

{done:IN_AID_OF_THE_MYREQUE,DARKNESS_OF_HALLOWVALE,SINS_OF_THE_FATHER} Drezel later works with the Myreque in In Aid of the Myreque, Darkness of Hallowvale and Sins of the Father.

sections.heading: Where it took us
sections.body:
Varrock Palace: King Roald's audience room, in the south-east corner by the main entrance. There is always a bucket in the palace bedroom.

Silvarea: the mountain pass in north-east Misthalin, past the Earth altar, ending at the temple.

Paterdomus: the temple on the River Salve, held by the monks from the ground floor up, with Drezel's cell on the top floor.

The mausoleum: down the trapdoor north of the temple. The guardian's chamber, the seven-monument room with the well behind the southern gate, and the north-east passage where Drezel settles.

The River Salve: the blessed river that forms Misthalin's border with Morytania. The temple bridge is the only crossing.

Morytania and Canifis: the werewolf town just east of the temple, and the land beyond it, both opened by the quest.

Varrock Museum: Historian Minas and the Kudos.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
The Seven Priestly Warriors have their own page, where I wrote their names out in full, and Morytania has its own, history and all.

{done:THE_BLOOD_MOON_RISES} The blessing on the Salve was not what the soldiers were told.

Wolfbane: "A silver dagger that can prevent werewolves changing form." The citizens of Canifis turn into werewolves when attacked, unless you wield it. It cannot be poisoned, you can only hold one, and Drezel replaces it.

{done:NATURE_SPIRIT} Drezel next sends you into Mort Myre Swamp with meat and apple pies for the druid Filliman Tarlock, in Nature Spirit.

One loose end. If you carry a clue scroll that wants Drezel, he sees to the clue in the mausoleum before he gets on with the quest. It does not matter much. It is true, so it stays.

people: Monk of Zamorak - level 30, the hooded impostor at the door
Temple Guardian - level 30, the dog in the mausoleum
Historian Minas - did not ask to see my notes. Nobody does.
details: Rewards - 1 quest point, 1,406 Prayer experience, Wolfbane, and the way into Morytania
Kudos - 5, from Historian Minas
Bucket - 2 coins at the general store
Essence - 50 rune or pure, in one trip with pouches or several without
Monuments - golden pot, feather, candle, tinderbox, needle and hammer
Souvenirs - one swap, before Drezel moves
Wolfbane - strikes like a mithril dagger, with a 5 Prayer bonus on top
Wolfbane - a silver weapon, so it works on tier 1 vampyres
Wolfbane - a Canifis citizen killed with it counts for the Easy Morytania Diary
Nature Spirit - also needs The Restless Ghost
Needed for - Animal Magnetism, Creature of Fenkenstrain, Desert Treasure I, Ghosts Ahoy
Needed for - Haunted Mine, His Faithful Servants, Making History, Nature Spirit, Rum Deal
Needed for - Shades of Mort'ton, Wanted!

plates.hint: Stop by the temple and I'll draw it.

entries.name: Waterfall Quest
entries.summary: Almera asked you to fetch her son Hudon back from treasure hunting on the river at Baxtorian Falls. You never did get him home, but you found the treasure he was after, so I have filed the errand as a success, loosely.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.body:
Almera was worried about her son Hudon. He cannot swim, and had already fallen in three times. You took her log raft, which wrecked on a small island, and there he was. He refused to come home, said he would find the treasure soon, and turned down your help on the grounds that you would only steal it.

You swam south and washed ashore by the Tourist Information Centre. Gerald and Hadley tell the story between them: an ancient elven king who shut himself in his secret home under the waterfall after his wife was captured and killed by invaders.

Upstairs was the Book on Baxtorian, which you had to read, and I read over your shoulder. It says Baxtorian and Glarial were elves, that a treasure lies under the falls, and that Glarial's pebble, the key to her tomb, was taken by a gnome family over a century ago. Their descendants might still keep it in their cave beneath the Tree Gnome Village.

Down in that cave the gnome Golrie had locked himself in to keep the hobgoblins off his family's heirlooms, and had left the key outside. You found it in a crate and let him out. He handed over Glarial's pebble as a bit of old elven junk, keeping the key so he could lock up again.

The tombstone says Glarial, wife of Baxtorian and a true friend of nature, rests knowing only visitors with peaceful intent may enter, and it means it: the pebble only opens the tomb if you carry no weapons, armour, runes or ammunition.

Inside, three Moss Guardians roam alongside zombies and skeletons, and you slipped past them unarmed, which was the sensible way to do it. You took Glarial's amulet and her urn, holding her ashes, and the tomb will not let you leave without both.

Then back to Almera's, the raft again, and the wreck again. Wearing the amulet is what stops the door on the waterfall ledge washing you out.

The final chamber holds six pillars, two statues and the Chalice of Eternity, floating in the air. You used one air, one water and one earth rune on each of the six pillars, Glarial's amulet on the statue of Glarial, and the urn on the chalice, tipping her ashes in. The ground rose. I put the quill down for that part.

Baxtorian's treasure was yours. Try to take it without the ritual and you are washed out of the cavern, and you lose the amulet and the urn. As for Hudon, the errand itself: he still has not found anything, accuses you of stealing his treasure, and insists you owe him a share, since he showed you where the treasure was.

sections.heading: Who was there
sections.body:
Almera: described, and fairly, as "Nice hair." Speedy Keith gets the very same words. I checked twice.

Hudon: described as "Looks young." I have not warmed to him.

Gerald: described as "Looks suspiciously like a fisherman." Fishes trout and salmon by the River Dougne. He knows the story of the treasure said to have been left by Baxtorian about 200 years earlier, at the end of the Fourth Age, and that many adventurers have searched for his tomb and failed. He was glad of someone to tell it to.

Hadley: described, not by me, as "Could do with losing a bit of weight." The tourist guide at the Tourist Information Centre.

{done:DESERT_TREASURE_I} He turns up again in Desert Treasure I, helping to find the Shadow Dungeon.

Golrie: described as "He seems to be in a spot of bother." A gnome of the Tree Gnome Village, and the current keeper of his family's heirlooms, Glarial's pebble among them until you came along.

{done:TREE_GNOME_VILLAGE,THE_PATH_OF_GLOUPHRIE} Golrie is the grandson of King Bolrie and grand-nephew of King Bolren, who rules the Tree Gnome Village and fights General Khazard's army in the quest of that name.

Baxtorian: King Baxtorian, the elven king under the falls, and Glarial's husband. You do not meet him.

{done:SONG_OF_THE_ELVES} In Song of the Elves he turns out to be alive, turned to stone in the hope of one day reuniting with Glarial; he is freed and, reluctantly, becomes elder of the Cadarn clan. He is Lord Baxtorian Cadarn now. He and Glarial had a daughter, Eirlys.

Glarial: Queen Glarial, wife of Baxtorian. The elves later buried her ashes in the tomb under the protection of the Moss Guardians.

{done:ROVING_ELVES} Taking her urn left her spirit restless until Roving Elves, and that one is on us.

sections.heading: Where it took us
sections.body:
Almera's house: north-east of Baxtorian Falls, south of the Barbarian Outpost, with the river behind it and the raft beside it.

Baxtorian Falls: the rapids themselves, which have their own page, barrel and all. The small island is where the raft wrecks. Both times.

Tourist Information Centre: just south of the falls by Lake Baxtorian. Hadley inside, Gerald fishing outside, the Book on Baxtorian upstairs in the southernmost bookcase on the east wall.

Tree Gnome Village: south-west of Ardougne and north of Yanille, hidden inside a hedge maze.

Tree Gnome Village Dungeon: down the ladder in the maze. The east room has zombies, giant bats and the key, in the differently coloured crate in the south-east corner; the west room has Golrie and the hobgoblins.

Glarial's Tomb: south-east of the falls, north-west of the Fishing Guild, under a tombstone. The amulet is in the west chamber's chest, the urn in the south chamber's coffin.

Waterfall Dungeon: the connected caverns under the falls, reached by rope from the big grey rock downstream to a dead tree and the doors on the ledge. The eastern passage has spiders, skeletons and the key in the northernmost crate; the western has fire giants and the locked door through to the chalice room, the northernmost cavern.

Barbarian Outpost and Fishing Guild: the landmarks either side of the falls. Good for bearings.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
{done:SONG_OF_THE_ELVES} The reason for the sealed door is the Elven Civil War. After the God Wars Seren shattered herself, and Baxtorian and Glarial were entrusted with leading the elves. Baxtorian took the Cadarn clan, the military clan, east through the Arandar pass to found a kingdom in what is now Kandarin.

{done:SONG_OF_THE_ELVES} He made non-aggression pacts with the gnomes and humans, and the kingdom prospered for nearly 1,900 years. Around 1930 of the Fourth Age, contact with Tirannwn ceased. The Iorwerth clan had seized Prifddinas while most of the army was away, leaving thousands dead.

{done:SONG_OF_THE_ELVES} They had become obsessed with a Dark Lord, who the elves believed was Zamorak but who turns out to be a fragment of Seren. Baxtorian spent five years besieging the city, whose walls Seren had built to withstand gods. His soldiers found a secret entrance and rescued the imprisoned clan elders.

{done:SONG_OF_THE_ELVES} Meanwhile his eastern kingdom, which Glarial ruled while he marched on Prifddinas, fell to invaders. Most of his people were slaughtered, and Glarial was taken and never recovered alive. He chased her captors into caves south of the ruined kingdom, into what was clearly a trap, and lost his remaining soldiers.

{done:MOURNINGS_END_PART_I,SONG_OF_THE_ELVES} Broken, he sealed himself in the home he had built for Glarial beneath the falls. The other elders reverted Prifddinas to a crystal seed, and Lletya was founded as a refuge under Arianwyn.

{done:ROVING_ELVES,SONG_OF_THE_ELVES} The war ended in year 169 of the Fifth Age with Song of the Elves, where Prifddinas is restored and Lord Iorwerth dies. On who took Glarial, the accounts disagree. The account of Glarial calls her captors unknown enemies, the account of the war says human invaders, and Islwyn in Roving Elves blames humans for her death. I have kept all three.

The book deserves its own note. Its own title is The Missing Relics, and it is described as "A book on elven history in northern Gielinor." It says many elven relics were lost when the elves left in the Fourth Age.

It also says dwarf miners may have taken Baxtorian's treasure early in the Fifth Age, and rumours say the same. And it says only Baxtorian and Glarial had the power to enter the falls, and the enchantment has kept everyone else out.

Inside is a sonnet on the love between Baxtorian and Glarial, which lasted over a century while they taught the laws of nature. There is also Baxtorian's own Ode to Eternity, on which I offer no opinion. The book can be displayed in your own house.

{done:SONG_OF_THE_ELVES} The book can also be read in the Grand Library of Prifddinas.

There is a section on their power over nature, commanding trees to grow, hills to rise and rivers to flood, with Baxtorian a master of rune lore who used stones to control water, earth and air. That is why the pillars take air, water and earth runes.

{done:ROVING_ELVES} Roving Elves picks the story up. Glarial gets a new resting place in the Waterfall Dungeon, consecrated with a seed from a Moss Guardian, which has its own page. Islwyn, her grumpy grandson, and the kind young elf Eluned scout for the rebel elves in Isafdar.

Golrie hands out a new pebble if yours is lost, and turns up again in The Path of Glouphrie.

{done:ROVING_ELVES} Once Roving Elves starts, he and the hobgoblins swap places, and the word on him becomes "No longer locked in his own cage."

{done:BIOHAZARD,REGICIDE} The Chalice comes up again in Biohazard, where King Lathas claims his brother Tyras was corrupted when the Dark Lord forced him to drink from it. That is a lie, and I have it written down as one, told to turn you against Tyras. There is no evidence the Chalice has anything to do with the Dark Lord.

Odds and ends from the margin. Glarial's amulet looks identical to the gnome amulet, and the dungeon's fire giants are the old reliable source of rune scimitars. For the minutes: once you have both the quest and the medium Kandarin Diary behind you, no rope is needed.

Fire giants - level 86, eleven of them in the western passage
Shadow spiders - level 52, drain Prayer, not shown on the map
Skeletons - level 45, in the eastern passage
Skeleton Mages - level 16, in the eastern passage
Hobgoblins - level 28, in the gnome dungeon
details: Requirements - no skills, and it can be done at level 3
Rewards - 2 diamonds, 2 gold bars, 40 mithril seeds and 1 quest point
Experience - 13,750 Attack and 13,750 Strength, 1 to 30 in both
Level 3 to 22 - what the experience alone does for a new adventurer
Needed for Desert Treasure I, Legends' Quest and The Path of Glouphrie
Needed for Roving Elves, along with Regicide
Needed for the medium Kandarin Diary

entries.name: Giant Mole
entries.summary: A mole the size of a hay cart, living in the tunnels under Falador Park. Wyson the gardener grew it by accident with a bottle of growth potion, which is the kind of accident I keep notes on.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
The Giant Mole, or Talpidae wysonian if you want the scientific name, after Wyson. A fairly simple fight as these things go. The note on it just reads "Holy Mole-y!" I did not write that.

Its main trick is to burrow off through the tunnels when it is hurt. It also puts out any candle, torch or oil lamp you are carrying if it comes up close enough to reach you. Annoying, but consistent.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body:
The Mole Hole, under Falador Park. Dig with a spade on one of the mole hills in the park and you drop straight in.

The tunnels are dark. Without a light you will be hurt as you walk them, so bring one.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
The histories put its origin down as a slight accident. Wyson poured a bottle of Malignius-Mortifer's-Super-Ultra-Flora-Growth-Potion on his plants. The name of the potion should have been a warning.

Wyson trades the mole's skins and claws for bird nests, which is a tidy arrangement for the man who caused the problem.

details: Level 230
Three tiles across
Always drops a mole skin and a mole claw
One kill completes a hard Falador Diary task

plates.caption: Falador, with a mole under it.
plates.hint: Stop in west Falador; I'll draw it.

entries.name: King Black Dragon
entries.summary: In the old days this dragon was the strongest creature known, and it is the size of a house. Its lair sits behind a lever in the deep Wilderness, which tells you most of what you need to know.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
People describe it as "One of the biggest, meanest dragons around." They are not exaggerating. It will set on you unprovoked and its bite poisons.

It has four breaths: ordinary dragonfire, then shock, ice and poison. Its weakness is water spells, which seems fair for something that breathes fire.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body:
The King Black Dragon Lair, reached through the deep Wilderness near the Lava Maze. Climb down the ladder near the lesser demons, then pull the lever surrounded by poisonous spiders. The lair itself is not Wilderness. The approach very much is.

Common routes in: a burning amulet to the Lava Maze, the lever north-west of Ardougne Castle to the Deserted Keep, the Edgeville canoe, or the Wilderness obelisks. 50,000 coins buys you the lair to yourself. Steep, but nobody else gets a swing at your dragon.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
It was the strongest creature anyone had met until the Kalphite Queen turned up. I have that in the margin, underlined.

{done:A_TAIL_OF_TWO_CATS} It can talk. In A Tail of Two Cats it holds a conversation with Bob the cat, and gets interrupted before it finishes. I would have liked the minutes of that one.

people: Krystilia - her black dragon tasks do not count it. Check before you set off.
details: Level 276
Always drops dragon bones and two black dragonhide
Rare: KBD heads one in 128, dragon pickaxe one in 1,000
Rarer still: prince black dragon pet one in 3,000, draconic visage one in 5,000
Lair to yourself, 50,000 coins

entries.name: Goblin
entries.summary: The war god Bandos brought goblins to the world, and they are among its most common low-level creatures. Their main village in Asgarnia is run by two generals who cannot agree on anything, and somehow it still stands.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: The word on them is "An ugly green creature." Blunt, but not wrong. New adventurers learning to fight go looking for them, which is a polite way of putting it.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body:
Everywhere a new adventurer is likely to tread. Lumbridge alone has over a hundred of them, and there are more between Lumbridge and Varrock, west of Varrock, at the Digsite, Port Sarim, Draynor Village and Lumbridge Swamp.

Further afield too: the Goblin Cave, near the Fishing Guild, the Tree Gnome Village maze, the Clock Tower Dungeon, Hosidius, the Kebos Lowlands, the Hollows, the Observatory Dungeon and the Underground Pass. You are never far from one.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
Goblins follow Bandos, the Big High War God. He arrived on Gielinor in the Second Age to wage war, and brought armies of goblins, ogres, orks and ourgs with him. Goblins are not strong. They make up for it with numbers, which is the oldest trick there is.

The generals of Goblin Village are Bentnoze and Wartface. They butt heads over trivial things, armour colours among them.

{done:GOBLIN_DIPLOMACY} Settling that argument is the whole of the quest Goblin Diplomacy. Diplomacy is a generous word for it.

{done:THE_LOST_TRIBE,LAND_OF_THE_GOBLINS} Not all goblins stayed loyal to Bandos. The Dorgeshuun cave goblins rejected his doctrines and went back to the cooperative ways of their Yu'biusk past. Sensible, and rare.

people: General Bentnoze - of the Thorobshuun tribe. One half of the argument.
General Wartface - of the Garagorshuun tribe. The other half.
places: {done:THE_LOST_TRIBE,DEATH_TO_THE_DORGESHUUN} Dorgesh-Kaan - home of the Dorgeshuun cave goblins
details: Most are level 2, with 5 hitpoints
The armed ones are level 5
The tougher sort are level 13

entries.name: Hill Giant
entries.summary: A very large foe, found in dungeons and hills across Gielinor. The weakest of the three giant kinds most adventurers meet first, which is not the same as weak. Their giant keys open the door to Obor, the Hill Titan.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: The Kourend sort are said to be "A very large foe that has been corrupted by the Dark Altar", which is the same giant in a worse neighbourhood. Now and then one leaves more than bones behind. Worth checking the pile.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body:
The Edgeville Dungeon has the most of them close to home. The Shayzien Giant Pit has more still.

Also in the Giants' Den, the Catacombs of Kourend, the Giants' Plateau, Taverley Dungeon, the Deep Wilderness Dungeon, the Lava Maze, the Gnome Maze, north of the Observatory, south-west of the Tree Gnome Stronghold, the Bone Yard and the Avium Savannah.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
The old histories just call them Giants. The hill was put on the front of the name to keep them apart from the other giant kinds, and it is said the hill is for their arm muscles, which resemble hills. I have looked. I suppose they do.

Despite the name, most of them live in dungeons. Some carry cleavers. The other two of the three kinds are moss giants and ice giants.

{done:RECIPE_FOR_DISASTER} The cleavers some hill giants carry are weapons from Recipe for Disaster.

places: Edgeville Dungeon - 12 of them
Giant Pit - 13 of them
Catacombs of Kourend - home of the Dark Altar corrupted sort
Giants' Plateau - has its own sort of hill giant
details: Level 28
Always drop big bones
Now and then a giant key
Now and then a giant champion scroll, for the Champions' Challenge

entries.name: Fire giant
entries.summary: The strongest of the ordinary giants, an elemental brute living in the Brimhaven Dungeon and a good many other caves. A favourite Slayer and Ranged target, and the classic source of a rune scimitar. Everyone goes back eventually.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Described as "A very large elemental adversary." Understated. There are three sorts, all of them aggressive and none of them quick to swing. Nothing burns it, and water magic bites. No surprises on either count.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body:
{done:WATERFALL_QUEST} The Waterfall Dungeon has eleven. They guard Baxtorian's western passage and the chalice room.

The Brimhaven Dungeon, the Catacombs of Kourend, the Charred Dungeon, the Deep Wilderness Dungeon, the Giants' Den, the Isle of Souls Dungeon, the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon, the Smoke Dungeon and the Stronghold Slayer Dungeon all keep them.

Most of those spots have a corner it cannot reach you in. The Charred Dungeon is the only one where more than one can set on you at once, so mind yourself there.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body: The drop that matters is the rune scimitar. Beyond that: the fire battlestaff, the steel axe, the mithril square shield, fire and chaos runes and the odd gem.

details: Level 86 - 111 hitpoints, hits up to 11
Levels 104 and 109 - the other two sorts
Rune scimitar - rare, about 1 in 128
Slayer - no level needed, and Slayer masters assign them

entries.name: Monk of Zamorak
entries.summary:
Evil human clerics of Zamorak. Weak on paper, but the paper is wrong.

{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} A band of them seized Paterdomus in Priest in Peril and poisoned the River Salve, which tells you the sort.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Described as "An evil human cleric." Brief, and fair. They switch between melee and magic and hit harder than their level suggests.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body:
The Chaos Temple in Asgarnia, the cage under the stairs in Varrock Palace, Taverley Dungeon and the Deep Wilderness Dungeon.

{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} Paterdomus too, the temple on the River Salve, all through Priest in Peril; they had the run of the place.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} At Paterdomus the hooded one at the door passed himself off as Drezel, the priest they had imprisoned. The rest is on the Priest in Peril page.

{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL,THE_BLOOD_MOON_RISES} The ones at Paterdomus heal quickly and are poor value, and they were cleared out for good in The Blood Moon Rises, which took a while.

Many an adventurer trains magic on the caged one in Varrock Palace with the Curse spell. He is in no position to object.

people: Zamorak - the god they serve. Chaos, by trade.
details: Levels 17, 22, 23, 30 and 45
{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} The hooded one at Paterdomus - level 30
Bones - always
Zamorak monk top and bottom - about one in twenty each
{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} Paterdomus monks - 25 percent of normal combat experience

entries.name: Temple Guardian
entries.summary: A big dog in the mausoleum under Paterdomus, on the River Salve. Worth a page, I thought.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Described, and fairly, as "Looks like a big ugly dog." It stabs, and quickly. Rings of recoil will do the job, so long as you land at least one hit yourself.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body: Below Paterdomus, the temple on Misthalin's eastern border, down the trapdoor north of it. It turns up only during Priest in Peril. Found once, then.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} By King Roald's account it guarded the way into the mausoleum and the river's source. The rest belongs to Priest in Peril, which has its own page.

{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} Roald called it Spots. He also called it a pedigree light beast, or was it dark beast. His words, not mine.

It is said that Dark beasts once looked much like it, only brown. Make of that what you will.

people: {done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} King Roald - its owner
details: Level 30 - 45 hitpoints, hits up to 3
Immune - magic and dwarf cannons
Slayer - counts among the dogs, for what that is worth

entries.name: Moss Guardian
entries.summary:
The guardian spirits of Glarial's Tomb, and a good deal stronger than the ordinary moss giant.

{done:ROVING_ELVES} In Roving Elves, Islwyn and Eluned send you to kill one bare-handed for a consecration seed. Bare-handed, noted.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Described as "Bigger than your average moss giant." Slow to swing, and always aggressive. Each blow is tried as ordinary melee first. If that misses, it is tried again against your magic defence. Protect from Melee stops only the first part. Underlined.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body:
Glarial's Tomb, south-east of Baxtorian Falls and north-west of the Fishing Guild, under a tombstone. Three of them, and nowhere else.

{done:WATERFALL_QUEST} The tomb admits no weapons, armour, runes or ammunition, so they are met with bare hands. Bring food, and potions.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body: They guard Glarial, the queen whose tomb it is. The Waterfall Quest has its own page.

details: Level 84 - 120 hitpoints, hits up to 14
Attack, Strength and Defence - 60 each
Drops - big bones
{done:ROVING_ELVES} Consecration seed - dropped only during Roving Elves

entries.name: Lumbridge
entries.summary: A large town in Misthalin, where everyone begins and where the dead come back, so it gets a lot of traffic. It is named for the bridge over the River Lum. Duke Horacio rules from the castle.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
Tutorial Island sends its new arrivals here, and the dead come back here too, unless they have arranged otherwise. So most people see it at least twice, once on the way in and once after the first mistake.

Duke Horacio is a direct descendant of Polonius, the first Duke, who was given the land by King Claudius of Varrock and replaced the original wooden fort with Lumbridge Castle. It is the kind of thing a duke likes written down, so I have.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body: South of Varrock, east of Draynor Village and west of Al Kharid, with Lumbridge Swamp and its caves to the south. Landmarks: the castle, the church of Saradomin, the cow field and the general store.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
{done:THE_LOST_TRIBE} During the God Wars, the caves beneath what is now the town sheltered a lost goblin tribe.

Long after the God Wars, migrating human nomads settled on the River Lum. They built a bridge across it, then named the town after the bridge. Practical people. Good bridge.

Father Aereck keeps the church of Saradomin, which is over 230 years old and still standing. Four quests start here too: four scrolls from one town with one bridge.

{done:LOST_CITY} An unassuming shed in the swamp leads to the fairy city of Zanaris. I would not have guessed from the shed.

people: The Lumbridge Guide - helps new adventurers and turns up in several quests
details: Founded - the year 1937 of the Fourth Age
{done:LOST_CITY} The shed to Zanaris - opens once Lost City is done
Quests - Cook's Assistant, The Restless Ghost, Sheep Shearer, Rune Mysteries

plates.caption: Lumbridge, done in a hurry.
plates.hint: Stop in Lumbridge and I'll draw it.

entries.name: Varrock
entries.summary: The capital of Misthalin and one of the largest cities in Gielinor. It began as Avarrocka, a forest camp. Loud, busy, and I am fond of it.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
Varrock is said vah-ROCK. King Roald resides in Varrock Palace, the city's focal point. You cannot miss it, though people try.

The Grand Exchange stands inside the walls, and so do a Saradomin church and a Zamorakian chapel. Both faiths, one set of walls. I have not asked how that works.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body: Central Misthalin. The Wilderness lies to the north, Barbarian Village to the north-west, the Digsite to the east and Lumbridge to the south.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
Avarrocka began when a nomadic tribe found a boy of exceptional strength, took him for a good omen and settled in the forest there. The boy was Arrav, and as he grew, so did Avarrocka.

{done:DEFENDER_OF_VARROCK} Ten years after the founding, goblins attacked. The boy defeated them, and that is where the name Arrav comes from.

{done:SHIELD_OF_ARRAV,DEFENDER_OF_VARROCK} Zemouregal, a Zamorakian Mahjarrat necromancer, later invaded with an army of zombies. His forces were beaten, but Arrav fell and was taken as an undead servant. A poor ending for the boy. The city rebuilt, grew into the kingdom of Misthalin and became a monarchy.

Avarrocka has shortened to Varrock, and the boy has not been forgotten. The Shield of Arrav still figures in city lore. Seven quests start here. A busy notice board, and I have stood at it a while.

people: King Roald - ruler of Misthalin
places: Grand Exchange - the great trading floor
Varrock Museum - natural history displays and a quiz
Champions' Guild - sells rune weapons and green dragonhide
Blue Moon Inn - the most popular pub in Varrock
Varrock Sewers - home of Scurrius and Bryophyta
details: Founded - the year 700 of the Fourth Age, as Avarrocka
Quests - Demon Slayer, Dragon Slayer I, Romeo & Juliet, Shield of Arrav
More quests - Defender of Varrock, Family Crest, Priest in Peril

The Exchange. I bought nothing.

entries.name: Paterdomus
entries.summary:
The temple of Saradomin on the River Salve, at Misthalin's eastern edge. It is the only gate into Morytania.

{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} It stands over the graves of the Seven Priestly Warriors. I lower my voice in there.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
The name comes from an old tongue, pater plus domus. House of the Father, meaning Saradomin.

{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} You need Drezel's blessing to cross its bridge, and he is the temple's only priest, so there is no one else to ask.

{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} Four floors: an altar on the ground floor, a cell and a vampyre coffin at the top, and monks of Zamorak on every floor from the ground up. Not what you expect in a house of Saradomin, but there it is.

{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} Outside are more coffins. They hold vampyres stranded west of the river, too weak to move and impossible to kill, which is a combination I do not care for.

There is a statue of Saradomin by the water, and a railing shortcut. A trapdoor to the north leads down to the basement mausoleum.

{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} Down there are the guardian's chamber, a well ringed by seven monuments, and a passage to the north-east.

{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL,IN_AID_OF_THE_MYREQUE} There is a hidden library down there as well.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body: In eastern Silvarea, the pass that leads to it, on the River Salve. Canifis is just across the river.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
{done:PRIEST_IN_PERIL} The Seven Priestly Warriors blessed the Salve here, and the temple was built in their honour. The monuments round the well in the mausoleum are theirs, so I mind where I stand. They have their own page.

It features in Priest in Peril, Nature Spirit, In Aid of the Myreque, Darkness of Hallowvale, Sins of the Father, Devious Minds and The Blood Moon Rises. A great many scrolls pass through this door. Mine included.

details: Railing shortcut - 65 Agility
Temple Trekking - the finish line

plates.caption: The temple on the Salve.
plates.hint: Stop by the temple and I'll draw it.

plates.caption: Drezel. The King asked after him.

entries.name: Baxtorian Falls
entries.summary: Rapids in Kandarin, running south from the Lunar Sea to the River Dougne, north-west of Ardougne. Named for the elven king who sealed himself beneath them, which tells you something about the place.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
A stretch of rapids with a great deal packed around it, starting with Almera, who lives at the top, and her son Hudon, out on the island after treasure. Hadley's Tourist Information Centre and Gerald the fisherman are just south. Rasolo the merchant is by the centre, and overpriced. I checked.

There is a second waterfall that flows east from the lake. The west bank is for leaping-fish Barbarian fishing, and the whirlpool takes you down into the Ancient Cavern. On purpose, I am assured.

{done:WATERFALL_QUEST} Glarial's Tomb is a short way south-east, under a tombstone.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body: East of the Tree Gnome Stronghold and south of the Barbarian Outpost. Get there by games necklace, or on foot from Seers' Village if you want the walk.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body: {done:SONG_OF_THE_ELVES} The king in question goes by Lord Baxtorian Cadarn these days, and he is no longer under the falls.

details: Barbarian fishing - fast Fishing training, with a Barbarian rod
Ancient Cavern whirlpool - after Barbarian Training
Barrel - off the ledge and down the river, if you are the sort

plates.caption: The falls. The ink ran.
plates.hint: Stop by the falls and I'll draw it.

entries.name: Seven Priestly Warriors
entries.summary:
Seven priestly warriors of Saradomin in the Fourth Age, who held Lord Drakan's vampyres at the River Salve and blessed it so no vampyre could cross. It cost them their lives. Paterdomus now stands on the ground they held.

{done:THE_BLOOD_MOON_RISES} They were Temple Knights, and only six of them died in the fight itself.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
Their names: Ivandis Seergaze, Iriandul Caistlyn, Sarl Dunegun, Derygull Templeton, Erysail the Pious, Friar Twiblick and Essiandar Gar. I have written all seven names out in full. They earned that much.

They were active around 1200 of the Fourth Age, in the Misthalin-Morytania War, when Drakan had crossed the Salve and pushed west towards Varrock.

{done:THE_BLOOD_MOON_RISES} The Temple Knights sent them to secure the river. Secretly, they were also to research haemalchemy, which their leaders believed held the key to beating vampyres.

{done:THE_BLOOD_MOON_RISES} Their savants designed a blood ritual to bar vampyres from the river. The warriors hid its profane nature from the soldiers and called it a holy consecration by Saradomin. A blood rite with a clean name. It worked, which is the uncomfortable part.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
{done:THE_BLOOD_MOON_RISES} At the river's source the vampyres attacked mid-ritual. Derygull fell first, then the others, one by one, until only Ivandis was left. He laid the six to rest around the ritual well.

{done:THE_BLOOD_MOON_RISES,IN_AID_OF_THE_MYREQUE} Ivandis was showing signs of vampyrification. He refused to become what they had sworn to destroy, and charged into Morytania to kill Drakan. He died in the attempt, and his coffin lies in caves beneath the Hollows. I have no remark for that one.

Later histories say the blessing sealed the vengeful power of Saradomin in the river. Drezel of Paterdomus is descended from one of the seven.

{done:SINS_OF_THE_FATHER} Ivan Strom is Ivandis's last living descendant. That should be better known.

people: {done:IN_AID_OF_THE_MYREQUE} Ivandis Seergaze - from what is now Lumbridge
places: Silvarea - site of the last battle
details: Misthalin-Morytania War - about 1100 to 1200 of the Fourth Age

plates.caption: The temple over their graves.
plates.hint: Stop by the temple and I'll draw it.

entries.name: Morytania
entries.summary: A land of evil in the far east of Gielinor, ruled by Lord Drakan's vampyres. Only the blessed River Salve keeps the vampyres out of Misthalin, and I am fond of that river.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
The name is said mor-ee-TAY-nee-ah. The land is full of aggressive creatures, and Lord Drakan's vampyres rule it. None of the towns is restful, and the walks between them are no better than the stops.

{done:DARKNESS_OF_HALLOWVALE,A_TASTE_OF_HOPE,SINS_OF_THE_FATHER} Drakan's sister Vanescula calls him Lowerniel. She and their brother Ranis once ran things for him. Ranis is dead now, and Vanescula turned against him.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body: East of Misthalin, across the River Salve. The way in is the temple of Paterdomus on the river.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
{done:IN_AID_OF_THE_MYREQUE,DARKNESS_OF_HALLOWVALE,SINS_OF_THE_FATHER} Before the God Wars this was Hallowvale, or the Hallowland, a Saradominist kingdom under the Icyene Queen Efaritay. In the Third Age Lord Drakan conquered it with vampyres and werewolves. He turned the fertile land into swamp and kept its people as a blood farm. That is the history of the place in three sentences, and none of them get better.

{done:IN_SEARCH_OF_THE_MYREQUE,DARKNESS_OF_HALLOWVALE,SINS_OF_THE_FATHER} Drakan himself is a true-born vampyre, brought from Vampyrium by Zaros in the Second Age, who sided with Zamorak in exchange for these lands. He captured Efaritay's husband Ascertes, who became the vampyre Vanstrom Klause.

The Salve was blessed against Drakan's invasion by the Seven Priestly Warriors, who have their own page. Its water burns creatures of Zamorak on contact, and no vampyre can cross it. I check, every time.

Werewolves can still cross, and do, kidnapping people and smuggling for the vampyres; some have got as far as beneath the Champions' Guild. Roavar says Drakan's brother Draynor ended up trapped on the Misthalin side of the river.

{done:SINS_OF_THE_FATHER} Vanescula says Draynor was weak even before the Salve trapped him, and a coward as well. There was a reason, she says, that Lowerniel had him banished.

The Salve flows past where Senntisten once stood, and the Digsite excavations reach its bank. The river has more history than most kingdoms.

{done:HAUNTED_MINE} Blessed water seeping through the rock of the Mort Ridge Mine forms Salve shards, crystals with power over evil. The Salve amulet is made from one, and the undead do not care for it.

The Barrows brothers tried to liberate the land, and died for it. The Myreque now fight to throw off vampyre rule. I hope they get a longer page than the brothers did.
